Triage: lands in `docs/adr/0127-authorization-cache-invalidation-contract-and-ttl-bound.md`, carried by the `packages/plugins/plugin-auth` behaviour it describes; rationale: the anchoring rule routes on the fix's landing surface, and the two corrections are measurements of plugin-auth's door posture — `domain:services` owns that behaviour. `docs/adr/**` is governed surface for *landing* purposes (draft-only, human merge), which is a dispatch-side constraint, not a routing one; it is not on the `domain:skills` file list.

Type **Bug**: two statements of fact in a repo document are measurably false, and statement 1 has a demonstrated cost — it is the same false premise that mis-graded #12547 and bought that card a full retriage round.

State **`pm:blocked`**, not `pm:queue`, for a dependency the card does not itself state. The card establishes that #12547 does not depend on this fix; the reverse direction does hold. The sentence to be amended describes the guard posture of **both** doors, and #12547 is in flight changing the `cookieCache` door's posture — its PR lands a pin that goes red on a revoked session. Amending "the `cookieCache` door … is **unguarded**" before that pin lands produces a document that is false again in a new way within hours. Queue-labelling it now would tell the services seat this is dispatchable when it is not.

Blocked-by: #12547

Per the standing unlock discipline this line lives in a comment (body-escaping trap), and on release the card's file surface gets re-verified **on the merged ref** before it returns to the queue — that re-verify is load-bearing here rather than routine: the merge that closes #12547 is the most likely thing to have changed what these two sentences should say. Whoever picks it up then should re-read both statements against the post-merge tree rather than against this card's measurements.

Grading note for the services seat, carried as a **premise to falsify, not a fence**: the card's options A/B are a minimum-edit preference and neither touches an ADR *decision* — D7's ruling stands under all three. That keeps this out of the ADR-class manual floor. ⛔ Option C is not available: leaving a falsifiable-in-ten-minutes claim next to the one warning that must land (`secondaryStorage`, the unbounded door) is what teaches operators to read the real warning as boilerplate.

Dedup: searched ADR-0127 / session-cache door cards — no twin; #12547 is the code-side disclosure and is a different defect.

## Unlock — `Blocked-by: #12547` discharged. ⚠️ And the re-verify triage called load-bearing found a **third** false statement, created by the merge that unlocked this card.

`domain:services` seat, session `session_0194kbQJxUvv2yvsGRtuXpP5`, 2026-08-27. `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`.

**#12547 is closed / completed** (PR #12735 MERGED, verified by content at the time). Triage's unlock condition was not a formality:

> the merge that closes #12547 is the most likely thing to have changed what these two sentences should say. Whoever picks it up then should re-read both statements **against the post-merge tree** rather than against this card's measurements.

Done, on `origin/main` at `f75a38afa`. All three findings below are post-merge readings, ⛔ not this card's original measurements.

## Statement 1 — still false, and now the repo **contradicts it in terms**

`docs/adr/0127-…md:148`:

> The `secondaryStorage` door into D7's rejected architecture is **boot-refused and pinned**

PR #12735 landed a docblock in the very module the sentence is about — `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/secondary-storage.ts:47`:

> ⛔ **Neither door is boot-refused** by …

⇒ This is no longer an unmeasured claim sitting alone; it is a **direct textual contradiction between an accepted ADR and the shipped code's own docblock**, both on `main`. That is strictly worse than what this card was filed for, and it strengthens the case rather than weakening it.

⭐ **A likely origin for the original error, found while re-verifying** — `secondary-storage.ts:89` documents that `rateLimit.storage: 'secondary-storage'` *"throws at boot without it"*. That **is** a real boot throw, and it involves the words "secondary storage" — but it is a **rate-limit configuration requirement**, not a refusal of the session-cache door. ⚠️ Whoever amends this should say which throw is real and which is not, or the next reader re-derives the same wrong generalisation from the same evidence.

## Statement 2 — still false in magnitude

`:113`: *"`cookieCache` is a different key reaching the same architecture, **with the same result**."* PR #12735 landed a measured table showing the reach is materially smaller in three ways — the session of record stays in `sys_session`; the staleness window is bounded (`cookieCache.maxAge`, default 300s); it is force-disabled whenever a `database` is configured, which ObjectStack always does; and sensitive operations already bypass it. Right direction, overstated result.

## ⚠️ Statement 3 — NEW, and created by the unlocking merge itself

`:148` also says the `cookieCache` door is:

> **unguarded** (measured: zero occurrences repo-wide, so it is unconfigured rather than protected)

**Both halves are now false.** PR #12735 landed an observation pin in `session-of-record.test.ts` plus the cost disclosure in `auth-manager.ts`, so occurrences are no longer zero and the door is no longer merely "unconfigured".

⭐ Triage predicted this exact outcome as the reason to block rather than queue: *"Amending 'the `cookieCache` door … is unguarded' before that pin lands produces a document that is false again in a new way within hours."* ⇒ The block was correct, the timing was correct, and the re-verify is what caught the third statement. Had this card been queued on 08-27 morning, its fix would have shipped a document false in a new way — which is precisely what the card exists to stop.

## Grading — carried from triage, re-checked

- **Clause ② = `no`.** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` read live at `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs:3813`: `claude-fable-5`, not applicable. Amending prose changes no contract accept/reject behaviour and widens no public surface, and ⭐ **no ADR *decision* moves** — D7's ruling stands under every option, which keeps this off the ADR-class manual floor.
- ⛔ **`docs/adr/**` is governed surface**: draft PR only, ⛔ never flipped ready, ⛔ never enqueued, ⛔ never auto-merged. **The maintainer's merge IS the review record.** That is a dispatch-side constraint, not a routing one.
- ⛔ **Option C (leave it) remains unavailable**, per triage: leaving a falsifiable-in-ten-minutes claim next to the one warning that must land — `secondaryStorage`, the unbounded door — is what teaches operators to read the real warning as boilerplate.

- **Model**: `claude-opus-5` — clause-② `no` per the unlock note
- `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched`

## ⛔ The one fence that outranks everything else on this card

`docs/adr/**` is **governed surface**. **Draft PR only.** ⛔ Never flip it ready, ⛔ never enqueue it, ⛔ never arm auto-merge — including by this seat afterwards. **The maintainer's merge IS the review record**, and that is the whole point of the surface, not a formality to route around.

## Three statements to correct, all re-measured post-merge at `f75a38afa`

⛔ Do **not** work from the card body's original measurements — they predate PR #12735. Re-read each against the tree yourself; the unlock note (`5447281781`) has the citations.

1. **`:148` — "the `secondaryStorage` door … is `boot-refused and pinned`"** → false. ⭐ And the shipped code now says the opposite in terms: `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/secondary-storage.ts:47` reads *"⛔ Neither door is boot-refused by …"*. An accepted ADR and the module's own docblock currently contradict each other on `main`.
2. **`:113` — "`cookieCache` … reaching the same architecture, `with the same result`"** → wrong in magnitude. `auth-manager.ts` (landed by #12735) carries the measured table: session of record stays in `sys_session`; window bounded by `cookieCache.maxAge` (default 300s); force-disabled whenever a `database` is configured, which ObjectStack always does; sensitive operations already bypass it. ⚠️ The *direction* is right — ⛔ do not overcorrect into "harmless", which would be a new false statement in the opposite direction.
3. ⚠️ **`:148` — "`cookieCache` … is `unguarded` (measured: zero occurrences repo-wide, so it is unconfigured rather than protected)"** → **both halves now false**, and this one did not exist when the card was written. #12735 landed an observation pin in `session-of-record.test.ts` plus the disclosure in `auth-manager.ts`, so occurrences are not zero and the door is not merely "unconfigured".

⭐ **A likely origin of error 1, worth writing into the correction rather than just fixing silently**: `secondary-storage.ts:89` documents that `rateLimit.storage: 'secondary-storage'` *"throws at boot without it"*. That **is** a real boot throw and it involves the words "secondary storage" — but it is a **rate-limit configuration requirement**, not a refusal of the session-cache door. Say which throw is real and which is not, or the next reader re-derives the same wrong generalisation from the same evidence.

## Scope

- ✅ Amend the **Consequences** prose so all three statements are true against the post-merge tree, and cite the file+line each corrected claim rests on so a future version bump is re-checkable one grep at a time.
- ⛔ **No ADR *decision* changes.** D7's ruling stands under every option and must read identically after your edit. If you find yourself wanting to change what D7 decides, **stop and report** — that is the ADR-class manual floor and it is not this card.
- ⛔ **Option C (leave it) is not available.** Leaving a falsifiable-in-ten-minutes claim beside the one warning that must land — `secondaryStorage`, the *unbounded* door — is what teaches operators to read the real warning as boilerplate.
- ⛔ Never `content/docs/releases/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. ⚠️ On `packages/spec`: not measured either way — if the work reaches a spec file, stop and report.

## Verification

This is a prose change, so the usual suite proves little. What does apply:

- Re-derive the gate union live on your actual changed set (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`) and run every family it names — `check:governed-prose` and the docs-audit families are the ones that matter here. Quote each verdict line; capture exit codes **before** any pipe.
- ⭐ **The real check is adversarial re-reading**: for each corrected sentence, find the file and line that makes it true and quote it in the PR body. A correction you cannot cite is a second unmeasured claim replacing the first.
- ⛔ Never accept `pnpm --filter X run <script>` as a measurement without confirming `X` declares that script — a package lacking it matches nothing, runs nothing and **exits 0**.
- ⚠️ `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` is **NOT MEASURED**, never a pass or a fail.

## Deliverable

Push the branch and open a **draft** PR linking `Fixes #12734`, whose body quotes each old sentence, each new one, and the file+line evidence for the new one. Then return the structured JSON report. ⛔ Stop there — do not land it.

## PM review of record — **ACCEPT.** ⛔ PR #12835 stays **DRAFT**; the maintainer merges governed surface.

`domain:services` seat, session `session_0194kbQJxUvv2yvsGRtuXpP5`. ⛔ Not flipped ready, ⛔ not enqueued, ⛔ auto-merge not armed — and it will not be by this seat. **The maintainer's merge IS the review record.**

## ⭐ The finding is bigger than the card, and it should be the headline

The card was filed as *"two measurably-wrong facts."* What the dev found is that the old paragraph's **asymmetry was inverted**:

> The `secondaryStorage` door … is **boot-refused and pinned**; the `cookieCache` door … is **unguarded**.

⇒ It marked the **unbounded, reachable** door as handled, and pointed the alarm at the **bounded** one that ⛔ cannot even be reached through ObjectStack config. An accepted ADR was steering readers toward the wrong door. That is worse than two false sentences and is the real cost of leaving it — precisely the *"teaches operators to read the real warning as boilerplate"* failure triage named when it ruled option C unavailable.

The replacement inverts it back and says so in terms: `secondaryStorage` — *"reachable, and the unbounded one"*; `cookieCache` — *"bounded, and not reachable through ObjectStack config at all, by construction rather than by refusal."*

## Verified independently on the branch

**Diff surface**: one file, `+8/−2`. The **only** two removed lines are the two false sentences (`:113`, `:148`). ⇒ Nothing else in the ADR moved, so no other decision text could have.

⚠️ **A correction to my own check.** I first diffed the whole D7 section for byte-identity and it came back changed — which alarmed me until I read it. That check was **wrong by construction**: statement 2 *lives inside* D7's mechanism paragraph, so a correct fix must change bytes there. The dev's own instrument was better designed than mine (section sha **excluding the amended sentence**, plus a ruling-marker count of 6 before / 6 after). What I can verify and do: the removals are exactly the two target sentences, and the replacement **explicitly reaffirms** the ruling — *"⛔ Smaller is not harmless — a bounded window in which a revoked session still authenticates is a tolerance D4 never granted, so **D7's ruling covers this door too**."* D7 is preserved, not narrowed.

**The overcorrection fence held.** I fenced against turning "same result" into "harmless". The new D7 text keeps the failure **direction** intact and draws the line at **reach**: *"It is the reach the two doors do not share, not the direction."* And the `cookieCache` bullet ends *"⛔ That pin is a tripwire, not a rejection"* — so the pin is not oversold as a guard either.

**The origin-of-error note is written in, not fixed silently**, as instructed — the closing line names it: *"rather than … inferring a refusal from the rate-limit throw."* ⭐ And the dev went further than I asked: the default composition's boot throw is real, but it is **better-auth 1.7's, not this repository's**, reachable only because the OIDC provider is on by default — pinned by `session-of-record.test.ts:410` reaching the cache-backed store via `plugins: { oidcProvider: false }` and changing nothing else. That is a sharper account than "no refusal exists".

## Instrument discipline worth recording

⭐ **A positive control on a prose edit** — the hard part, because a green gate on a prose change proves nothing unless the gate is shown to *read the changed text*. A broken relative link was planted **inside the new paragraph**, the mutation proven on disk by blob hash before measuring, the gate went **red**, the restore was proven **by bytes** (blob back to the HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty), and the gate went green again.

**A declared divergence from my brief**: I predicted `check:governed-prose` + docs-audit families; the live derivation named `check:pm-governed-merges` and **no** docs-audit family. The dev followed the **live** derivation and ran my predicted families anyway as extras. ⇒ Correct order of authority — the live gate over the PM's guess — and it ran both rather than choosing.

**Two NOT MEASURED handled properly**: `check:doc-formula-expressions` returned `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` twice, was built through the shared verify lock, and re-run to a real exit 0 — never counted green while unmeasured. And one of its own greps read wrong first time (an unescaped `.` matching as a regex metachar), caught and re-measured with fixed strings.

⚠️ `packages/spec` was **read** for one citation and never edited — the fence was approached and correctly not crossed.
